title: Infera per-patch upstream status
description: One record per patch under deploy/docker/patches/. Lives beside the patch it describes, named <patch-file-prefix>.upstream.status.yaml. The patch's own header carries the full argument; this file is the machine-checkable index of where that patch stands against the project it patches.

schema_version.description: Bumped when this schema makes a breaking change.

status_updated.description: Date every upstream claim in this file was last checked. Upstream moves and this file does not, so a stale date is the signal to re-check rather than to trust.

verified_by.description: How the upstream claims below were established. 'gh-search' proves only that a title/body search missed — it does not prove absence. 'upstream-source-read' is stronger: the defect was confirmed present or absent by reading the upstream file.

path.description: Primary patch file, relative to the git root.

extra_files.description: Further files that are part of the same patch (a fragment appended by a script, a companion .diff).

kind.description: python-anchor-script and shell-script locate their target at run time and no-op on a miss; context-diff and git-diff fail loudly on ref drift.

idempotent.description: Re-running is a no-op. Absent means unknown, which for a patch that runs on every container start is a defect.

applied_by.description: Every surface that applies this patch. 'none' means carried but not wired up, which needs a reason in alive_because.detail.

opt_in_flag.description: Build ARG or env var that gates application, when it is not applied unconditionally.

library.description: The project whose source this patch edits — not the engine that runs it. A patch to vLLM's bundled MoRIIO connector has library 'vllm', component 'moriio'.

component.description: Subsystem inside that library: mooncake, moriio, hicache, dsa, disaggregation, hipfile, flydsl-moe, scheduler.

repo.description: owner/name on GitHub, or 'internal' for a closed-source engine.

files.description: Paths edited inside the target project, as the patch addresses them.

versions.description: Every pinned version of the target this patch is carried against. Two entries when a patch spans two engine bases — they can disagree about whether the defect is even present.

surface.description: Which build this version belongs to, when the patch spans more than one.

commit.description: Commit the ref resolves to. null only when the ref is genuinely unpinned, in which case unpinned_risk must say what that costs.

pinned_ref_on_main.description: Is the pinned commit an ancestor of the upstream default branch? false means a release branch, so upstream main fixes do not arrive by bumping a patch level. null for internal or unpinned targets.

release_branch.description: Upstream branch the pinned ref sits on, when it is not main.

unpinned_risk.description: Required in spirit when commit is null: what an unpinned target means for this patch.

digest_source.description: 'unresolved' means the Dockerfile pins the tag only; the digest is whatever the registry serves at build time.

value.description: Does the upstream default branch still carry the defect this patch fixes? null when there is no public upstream to check.

evidence.description: What settles it. Naming the file and line read from main is the standard here; 'no search hit' is not.

applies_to.description: Field 4a — what this patch actually does in each engine image it reaches.

surface.description: Dockerfile or runtime path this row is about.

effect.description: op = changes bytes and is load-bearing. no-op = reached but changed nothing (target absent, already fixed, or anchor gone). not-applied = never traversed on this surface. unverified = never checked on this surface, which is a gap, not a state.

required_to_run.description: true when the engine cannot serve the target workload without this patch.

alive_because.description: Field 4b — why we still carry this.

consumers.description: Which infera engines, images or workloads still need it. 'none' as the sole entry means the patch is a drop candidate on every surface.

drop_when.description: The concrete condition that retires this patch.

drop_signal.description: How we find out. 'base-version-only' and 'pin-advance-only' mean the patch keeps applying cleanly on a fixed base, so nothing fails and a human has to decide.

silent_misapply_risk.description: What goes wrong if this patch outlives its reason and nobody notices. Non-null whenever drop_signal cannot self-announce.

reason.description: Why it changed — not a restatement of the commit subject.

supersedes.description: Earlier patch files this one replaced.

upstream_issues.description: Field 7 — upstream issues for this defect. null is a legitimate value and must be written explicitly.

upstream_prs.description: Field 8 — PRs that fix, or claim to fix, this defect.

author.description: GitHub handle. null means not recorded — better than a placeholder, and note that `ours` can still be answered without it.

ours.description: Opened by a contributor of this repo.

same_approach.description: Does it fix the defect the way our patch does? null when it does not fix this defect at all and is listed for collision or context.

approach_note.description: Why ours differs, or why it does not. 'we needed a local narrow fix and are not carrying the general case' is a valid and useful answer.

requested_action.description: What an upstream maintainer explicitly asked for, and who asked.

in_pinned_base.description: Is this PR present in the version we actually build against? A merged PR that is not in the pinned base still needs the local patch.

related_refs.description: Field 9 — PRs and issues that do not decide whether we keep this patch but inform how it should be fixed: the same defect on another platform, a refactor that will move our anchor, a test that proves no CI covers this.

what.description: The defect, in one or two sentences.

why.description: Root cause — why the upstream code is wrong, not just what it does.

how.description: What the patch changes, and why that is the minimal correct change.

before_fix.description: Observed failure. Quote the error or the wrong output.

after_fix.description: Observed behaviour with the patch, measured where possible.

context.description: Which model, topology, arch and flags this reproduces under, and where it does not.

call_chain.description: Ordered path from entry point to failure site.

symptom_signature.description: The grep-able fingerprint — the exact assert, error string or fault address shape.

silent.description: true when the defect produces wrong results rather than a crash. These are the expensive ones.

verification.description: How the fix was established locally.

scope_limits.description: What this patch deliberately does not cover, so the next person does not assume it does.

open_actions.description: What still has to happen upstream or here. An empty list is fine; a missing PR of ours is not.

repo_path.description: Path relative to the git root, no leading slash and no '..'.

gh_ref.description: owner/name#123, or internal#123 for the private tracker.

note.description: What this reference tells us that the title does not.
